title: Spectral filtering and crystal length as control parameters for conditional correlations in quantum imaging
authors: Hashir Kuniyil, Asad Ali, Mohammadreza Rezaee, Saif Al-Kuwari
abstract: We establish spectral filtering as a control parameter for the conditional momentum and position correlations of SPDC biphotons used in quantum imaging. The conditional momentum uncertainty in spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) is strongly crystal-length and spectral-filter dependent along the walk-off axis; therefore, the effect is observed only in critically phase-matched (CPM) crystals such as $β$-barium borate (BBO) crystals, while quasi-phase-matched (QPM) crystals and the non-walk-off axis of BBO remain scaled strictly according to the standard pump waist size ($w_0$) dependent scaling law $1/w_0$-independent of the filter. In position space, the spectral-filter effect is universal and produces a flat-dip-rise (FDR) profile in every crystal class examined. Although this FDR profile was previously demonstrated in BBO only in the nondegenerate regime, our results establish its generality: the FDR dip is also present at exact degeneracy in QPM crystals, an unexpected feature that was previously thought to deliver a resolution advantage in the nondegenerate regime alone. Our treatment applies to all SPDC-based quantum-imaging regimes (including CPM and QPM crystals, walk-off and non-walk-off axes, degenerate and nondegenerate emission, and signal and idler filtering) and offers enhanced quantum-imaging resolution via the design rules presented-most prominently along the walk-off axis of CPM crystals (in far field) and across all transverse axes in the near field.
summary: This paper treats spectral filtering and crystal length as key controls for managing the conditional momentum and position correlations of biphotons from SPDC. It demonstrates that these parameters allow for enhanced quantum-imaging resolution by modifying correlation widths, particularly highlighting universal features like the Flat–Dip–Rise profile in position space.
main_problem: The study establishes spectral filtering and crystal length as controllable parameters governing the conditional momentum and position correlations of biphotons generated via Spontaneous Parametric Down-Conversion (SPDC) for quantum imaging.
main_result: Spectral filtering universally induces a Flat–Dip–Rise (FDR) profile in position space, and the achievable momentum correlation uncertainty can be significantly narrowed below pump-limited scaling, especially along the walk-off axis of CPM crystals.
method: The analysis uses point-to-point correlation estimation ($\sigma_{q_s|q_i=0}$) applied to the SPDC biphoton amplitude model, incorporating spectral filtering via Gaussian band-pass filters and analyzing far-field vs. near-field regimes.
model_or_system: The system is based on SPDC generating entangled/correlated photon pairs (signal and idler). The theoretical framework models the transverse spatial correlation using a paraxial approximation for phase matching, considering different crystal types like BBO (with walk-off) and QPM crystals.
key_observables: Conditional momentum uncertainty ($\sigma_{q_s|q_i=0}$), conditional position profile (FDR), and the spectral-filter dependent bandwidth ($\delta\lambda_{PM}$).
important_parameters: Spectral filter bandwidth ($\delta\lambda_{	ext{filter}}$), crystal length ($L$), pump waist size ($w_0$), and the type of phase matching (CPM vs. QPM).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the paraxial approximation for SPDC phase-matching, assumes a Gaussian pump envelope, and treats spectral filtering using Gaussian band-pass filters.
figures_summary: Not specified in detail, but the notes imply comparisons of $\sigma_{q|q_s=0}$ vs. $L$ (showing crossover scaling) and calculations of $\delta\lambda_{PM}$ for different crystal types and lengths.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes how spectral filtering modifies conditional correlations in SPDC, first detailing the momentum space control via walk-off effects in CPM crystals, then establishing the universal FDR profile in position space across various crystal classes (including QPM), and finally deriving bandwidths for phase matching under degenerate vs. non-degenerate conditions.
why_interesting: This work provides detailed quantitative rules for manipulating quantum correlations using spectral filtering, which is highly relevant to designing advanced quantum imaging protocols that require precise control over spatial entanglement properties.

(a) No-walk-off configurations (PPKTP Type-0, circles; Type-I, squares; BBO x axis, triangles) collapse onto the pump-set plateau 1/w0 = 2000 m−1, independent of both L and δλf. (b–d) BBO walk-off (y) axis. The walk-off term in ∆kz produces an L-dependence controlled by the filter through the dimensionless ratio R [Eq. (21)] at different filter bandwidths: (b) δλf = 3 nm, (c) δλf = 10 nm, and (d) δλf = 30 nm.

FIG. 2. Near-field conditional position uncertainty σxs|xi=0 as a function of the signal-arm spectral filter FWHM δλfilter in (a) PPKTP Type-I and (b) PPKTP Type-0, at fixed crystal length L = 3 mm, pump waist w0 = 500 µm, and pump wavelength λp = 405 nm. Three signal wavelengths are plotted in each panel; both crystals show a FDR profile at every signal wavelength, including the degenerate 810 nm case. Vertical markers in each panel illustrate the dip-position scaling Eq. (25) for the λs = 750 nm →λi = 880.4 nm conjugate pair.

FIG. 3. Phase-matching bandwidth versus signal wave- length at L = 3 mm, λp = 405 nm. Dashed curves: leading-order GVM expression Eq. (22), which diverges as λs approaches the degenerate point 2λp = 810 nm because |ng(λs) −ng(λi)| →0. Diamond markers: leading-order GVD-only value Eq. (26) at exact degeneracy. Solid curves: full second-order expansion [Eq. (26)] that keeps both the lin- ear GVM and quadratic GVD terms and is finite at all λs. The full expression smoothly bridges the two limiting regimes and at exact degeneracy reproduces the GVD-only marker to better than 0.05 nm.
